transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-21 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Mark Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Vale (Redwood CSM); Tom Chen (CTO), Anika Rao (Lead SRE), Luis Martinez (PM), Sara Kim (Security)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align staging pilot and network/runbook steps. Confirmed infra constraints (VPC peering), security gating (KMS + audit logs), and pilot success metrics (latency SLO, throughput). Agreed to a 2-hour staging smoke next week and to exchange runbook + network diagram.

Topics: network & VPC peering, data residency & KMS, Dedicated vs Hosted lanes for pilot, staging test plan, runbook ownership, success criteria (p95/p99 latency, cost target)

Transcript body:
[00:00:10] Mark Ellis: ok everyone thanks for jumping on, this is Mark from Redwood, um today we're doing the launchpad ignite — sorry — kickstart for the staging sherpa, we'll walk through the runbook, network, and the pilot scope
[00:00:25] Tom Chen: thanks Mark, excited, I'll hand to Anika to open with infra constraints, we have a couple of corporate firewall things and a strict CIDR map to stick to
[00:00:40] Anika Rao: yeah hi, hi, so key points: we need VPC peering with our staging account, no direct internet egress for inference nodes, and KMS integration for keys. also we have an onprem workload later so open to private deploy discussions but for pilot we want hosted or dedicated?
[00:01:05] Priya Nair: thanks Anika, from an SE perspective either Hosted or Redwood Dedicated works — for fastest time-to-value hosted is easiest, Dedicated gives you predictable throughput, isolation. for the pilot we usually do Redwood Hosted with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS when needed
[00:01:32] Luis Martinez: quick question — what are the tradeoffs on latency and cost if we go dedicated now versus hosted?
[00:01:45] Mark Ellis: good one — rough thumb: Dedicated will lower tail latency variance and give throughput guarantees at commit price, but it can be higher up-front. Hosted is more elastic and cheaper to get started but you may see higher p99 variance in noisy neighbor windows. Our console — Redwood Consolee — shows token-level cost and you can run a short bench to estimate
[00:02:10] Sara Kim: on security side we need SOC2 docs and an explanation on audit logs and retention, plus can you support customer KMS with automatic key rotation?
[00:02:25] Priya Nair: yes we support customer-managed KMS via our Private key integration (we often use KMS connectors). Key rotation policies are supported, we also capture audit logs with tenant-level export to your SIEM; i'll send the SOC2 package after call
[00:02:40] Tom Chen: great. can you share the runbook template?
[00:02:46] Mark Ellis: absolutely — i'll put a runbook draft in the shared drive. it's a short doc: network prep, secrets/KMS setup, sample requests for smoke, perf targets, and rollback steps.
[00:03:05] [00:03:05] Luis Martinez: sounds good, for success criteria we want p95 < 120ms and p99 < 300ms on typical queries, and cost per 1k tokens under our target — we can share baseline traffic patterns after
[00:03:24] Priya Nair: noted, we'll run a small synthetic with your qps shape. also we'll use KV cache and prefix caching which usually improves per-token cost and removes repetitive context cost — sometimes folks call it K-V cash in notes, fwiw
[00:03:45] Anika Rao: about network: we have strict egress rules so peering only; do you require NAT? we prefer no NAT for staging
[00:03:55] Priya Nair: we can do VPC peering, we typically ask for the peering and firewall rules so our routing can reach the inference endpoints. no NAT required if peering is provisioned and routes are allowed
[00:04:15] Mark Ellis: also quick note on model pinning and rollouts — you can pin versions and do canary rollouts; for pilot we'll suggest a canary at 10% traffic to observe latencies and regression on quality
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Sara Kim: two more security Qs — where do logs live, and how long do you keep request payloads by default?
[00:04:38] Priya Nair: default is 30 days for request logs in hosted, with options to extend; payload retention can be turned off for PII-sensitive flows and we can do on-prem package if you need air-gapped
[00:04:55] Tom Chen: ok that's helpful. timeline wise how fast can we go to a staging smoke test?
[00:05:02] Mark Ellis: if we get your peering info and accept a simple access form, we can spin staging in ~5 business days. Priya and I usually run the smoke with you and validate the runbook steps
[00:05:18] Anika Rao: that works. i can get CIDRs and firewall rules by monday, but need confirmation on IP ranges Redwood will use
[00:05:26] Mark Ellis: i'll include our peering IP ranges in the runbook doc, mark action: we will send it today.
[00:05:34] [00:05:34] Luis Martinez: question about private deployment — we might want private later, what does the onprem package look like?
[00:05:42] Priya Nair: onprem is a larger engagement — customer control plane with optional HSM integration, additional audit capabilities. it's usually a separate 계약, pardon contract, and takes longer to provision. for early tests we recommend hosted + customer KMS then plan private if you need full data residency
[00:06:05] Tom Chen: ok noted.
[00:06:10] [00:06:10] Jordan Vale: i'll be your onboarding CSM, i'll coordinate the runbook and milestones. we'll set a staging smoke next Tuesday morning, is that workable for Orbitline?
[00:06:22] Anika Rao: yes tuesday morning is ok for us, i'll make time
[00:06:28] Mark Ellis: perfect. sample staging test will be: connectivity check, auth/KMS signoff, run 10 min 50 qps load with your typical prompt distribution, collect p95/p99 and cost, rollback path validated
[00:06:46] Priya Nair: i'll prepare a simple k6 script and a lightweight client we can run from your side, plus an ingest harness to replay typical prompts if you share a small sample set
[00:06:58] [00:07:00] Sara Kim: about compliance handoff — we'll want to review the SOC2 and the encryption_at_rest details before we sign off on pilot
[00:07:08] Mark Ellis: understood; i'll attach SOC2 cert, dataflow diagram, and KMS integration doc. action item on me to share that today
[00:07:18] Tom Chen: can we also get an estimate on cost for the pilot? a one-week baseline number for hosted and for a small dedicated pool?
[00:07:27] Mark Ellis: yes i'll include a conservative cost estimate in the runbook, and Priya can run a short token-level bench once we have your sample prompts to refine the numbers
[00:07:40] Priya Nair: sometimes quantization and batching changes numbers a lot; we'll recommend quantization profile if latency and cost tradeoffs make sense for your model choice
[00:07:55] Luis Martinez: on model side we're planning to use a 7B open checkpoint tuned inhouse — any gotchas for that variant?
[00:08:03] Priya Nair: should be fine; we'll check compat and confirm optimal kernel selection. if you want lower latency we can test 4-bit quant with our runtime but we need to validate quality regressions with your eval set
[00:08:20] Tom Chen: quality regressions — let's be conservative for customer-facing flows. we can run eval sets as part of the pilot
[00:08:28] Priya Nair: perfect, include an eval suite in the repo and we'll tie regressions to canary fail conditions
[00:08:35] [00:08:35] Jordan Vale: recapping next steps — Mark will send runbook + IP ranges + SOC2 docs today, Anika will share CIDR/firewall by Monday, Priya will prepare the staging test harness and cost bench, Sara will review KMS/rotation needs and send any redlines
[00:08:54] Tom Chen: that matches our expectations. any blockers on the Redwood side?
[00:09:00] Mark Ellis: nothing major; just pending the policy forms and peering approvals. also want to call out fallback routing — if we see capacity issues in hosted we can failover to a cheaper model variant or dedicated pool per your policy, we can discuss autoscaling burst windows
[00:09:20] Anika Rao: autoscaling and predictable throughput are important, especially for peak shipment windows — how do we set burst policies?
[00:09:28] Priya Nair: we configure autoscale rules on Dedicated pools — you can set base capacity and burst to handle spikes. for Hosted we rely on runtime autoscaling plus routing policies, we can set a fallback rate limit to ensure your critical traffic keeps going
[00:09:47] [00:09:47] Luis Martinez: minor thing — will logs include token-level cost attribution for each request? that's useful for product analytics
[00:09:55] Priya Nair: yes per-request token counts and cost are available in the Console export, we can ship a daily CSV or integrate with your data lake via EDM export
[00:10:06] Mark Ellis: ok there's a few little admin things: we'll create a shared folder and invite Orbitline folks; i'll add the runbook, our IP ranges, the SOC2 PDF, and a short checklist template for the staging smoke
[00:10:22] [00:10:22] Tom Chen: thanks. anything else from Redwood?
[00:10:28] Priya Nair: just one technical ask — can you provide a small representative sample of prompts (50-100) and the expected outputs and latency targets per prompt class? that will help us tune batching and cache policy
[00:10:45] Luis Martinez: yes we can share that — i'll redact any PII and send by monday
[00:10:52] Sara Kim: and i'll coordinate the security review and let you know if we need additional attestations
[00:10:58] Mark Ellis: great. if no other points we'll close with a recap and i'll follow up with the sheet and links
[00:11:06] [00:11:06] Jordan Vale: recap: runbook + SOC2 + IP ranges (Redwood) by EOD, CIDR & firewall (Orbitline) by Monday, staging test prep (Priya) by Wednesday, KMS review (Sara) by Fri. schedule: staging smoke Tuesday next week 09:00-11:00 PST
[00:11:30] Tom Chen: confirmed, thanks everyone
[00:11:35] Mark Ellis: thanks all, talk soon

End of transcript.

Notes: shared artifacts referenced — runbook draft (link placeholder: https://redwood.app/drive/runbooks/orbitline-staging), SOC2 package (link placeholder: https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf), staging checklist sheet (spreadsheet link placeholder).
